title: Navigator Program: Career Operations and Onboarding Tooling
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Navigator Program: a cross-functional playbook that unifies onboarding, role alignment, micro-rotations, mentorship, and the internal tools and workflows people need to accelerate early-stage impact at Redwood. The Navigator Program is intended for new hires, managers, people-ops partners, and engineering/product leads who coordinate role progression and temporary assignments.

Purpose and goals:
- Reduce time-to-productivity for new hires and role-changers to < 8 weeks for core contributor paths.
- Provide a repeatable, equity-minded route for lateral moves, temporary rotations, and promotion-readiness reviews.
- Surface and standardize the tooling workflows needed for secure access, entitlement reviews, and benefits activation.
- Make skills and outcomes visible: objective checklists and transferable evidence for career conversations.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractors in engineering, product, and core platform teams.
- Includes: onboarding workflows (preboarding through 90 days), role alignment ladder templates, mentoring and sponsorship playbooks, micro-rotation process, benefits activation checklist, and internal tool access recipes.
- Excludes: compensation calibration process (see finance-and-legal), performance improvement plans (see people-ops/policies).

Key program components:
1) Navigator Phases (timeline and owner)
   - Preboarding (owner: people-ops): offer acceptance -> first day. Deliverables: account provisioning ticket created, manager welcome note, buddy assigned.
   - Day 0–14 (owner: manager + buddy): environment setup, first project task, security training, first 1:1 cadence established.
   - Day 15–60 (owner: manager): technical ramping, two documented code reviews, initial cross-team intro, quarterly benefits enrollment window guidance.
   - Day 61–90 (owner: manager + people-ops): impact review, promotion/readiness signal checklist, role-fit calibration meeting.

2) Role Alignment & Ladder Templates
   - Standardized components present in every role ladder doc: responsibilities, expected deliverables (30/60/90), measurable signals of success, examples of work, interview/assessment guidance.
   - Example (engineering IC path):
     * IC-2: owns small features, ~1–3 month scope, consistent pull request cadence, receives mentorship for design tradeoffs.
     * IC-3: independently owns medium features, mentors IC-2, leads design reviews, measurable SLO/bug impact ownership.
     * Staff/Principal: drives cross-team architecture, measurable cost/latency ownership, documented trade-off analyses.
   - Use the ladder template at: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/ladder-templates (related link).

3) Micro-rotation and Short-term Assignment Process
   - Purpose: let engineers and PMs try adjacent work for 4–12 weeks while preserving primary role responsibilities.
   - Steps:
     1. Employee submits Rotation Request form (internal link: /forms/rotation-request).
     2. Manager and receiving team lead approve timeline and objectives.
     3. People-ops creates a temporary entitlement plan: access, stipend adjustments, onboarding checklist for receiving team.
     4. Rotation kickoff doc created and shared in team wiki.
     5. Post-rotation debrief: outcomes, recommendation for next step.
   - Failure modes and mitigations: unclear objectives -> require SMART objectives; access delays -> escalate to platform access queue (SRE).

4) Mentorship, Sponsorship & Buddy System
   - Buddy: operational contact to help with day-to-day tooling and slack channels (assigned during preboarding).
   - Mentor: career and skill coach, recommended 1:6 ratio (mentors:mentees) for growth cohorts. Mentorship agreement should include 6 sessions over 3 months with agreed-upon goals.
   - Sponsor: manager or senior leader who advocates for stretch assignments and promotion-readiness. Nomination occurs during 60–90 day impact review if candidate shows potential.

5) Benefits and Perks Activation Checklist (concise)
   - Health & wellness: verify HR portal enrollment within 10 days of start.
   - Hybrid/office stipend: submit purchasing request with tagged receipts within 60 days.
   - Parental leave: notify people-ops with anticipated leave dates, schedule benefits briefing.
   - Education & training funds: request pre-approval from manager; expense via procurement.

6) Internal Tools Access Matrix and Onboarding Recipes
   - High-level matrix (examples):
     | Purpose | Tool | Default Role | Request Channel | Owner | SLA |
     |---------|------|--------------|-----------------|-------|-----|
     | Codebase | GitHub | read/write for team | GitHub access form | Eng-Auth | 2 business days |
     | Compute jobs | Kubeflow / Argo | dev-submit | infra Jira | GPU-Fleet | 3 business days |
     | Production tracing | Datadog | read for all engineers | Datadog request | Eng-SRE | 1 business day |
     | Customer data (prod) | Redact-DB | restricted | Data Access review | Security | 5 business days |
   - Onboarding recipe examples (CLI/commands and tickets):
     * Create new SS0 infra access: submit Jira ticket to ENG-ACCESS with project code and justification.
     * Provision local dev GPU images: run `./scripts/setup-dev.sh --cuda 12` then verify `nvidia-smi` and run smoke test `pytest tests/smoke --quick`.
     * Datadog trace sample: follow docs at /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/datadog-onboarding.

7) Manager & People-ops Responsibilities (checklist)
   - Manager:
     * Send welcome note within 24 hours of hire.
     * Run Week 1 and Week 4 1:1s focused on blockers and learning plan.
     * Assign measurable 30/60 tasks in the hiring manager template.
   - People-ops:
     * Verify all accounts provisioned by Day 3.
     * Schedule benefits orientation and send enrollment deadline reminders.
     * Maintain Navigator cohort calendar and mentor pool.

8) Promotion-Readiness Signals and Evidence
   - Recommended evidence items for promotion packet (ICs):
     * 3–5 production PRs with reviewer notes and impact numbers.
     * At least one cross-team project with measurable metric delta (latency, cost, reliability).
     * Two manager and peer attestations focusing on demonstrated leadership and ownership.
   - Promotion packet flow: submit to People-ops -> Calibration panel -> outcome and written feedback within 21 days.

9) Operational Metrics and Success Criteria
   - Metrics tracked monthly: time-to-first-PR, time-to-full-access, 90-day impact score (manager-rated), rotation-utilization rate, mentor satisfaction (survey).
   - Targets:
     * Time-to-first-PR < 14 days
     * Time-to-full-access < 10 days
     * 90-day impact score average >= 3.8/5

10) Rollout Plan and Retro Cadence
   - Pilot: Q2 2026 with 2 cohorts (engineering + product) for new hires and 8 micro-rotations.
   - Full rollout: Q4 2026 after pilot retros and tooling improvements.
   - Retro cadence: cohort retro at 30 days and program retro quarterly; maintain action tracker in Navigator Program home page.

11) FAQ and Troubleshooting
   - Q: My account provisioning is delayed beyond SLA. A: Escalate via `#infra-access` and open a Jira ticket with template tag NAV-ACCESS. People-ops will own the first escalation.
   - Q: Can I rotate into a team that is hiring? A: Yes, but rotations should not be used to bypass open hiring; if role interest persists post-rotation, follow internal hiring ladder and apply through internal transfers.

12) Templates and Examples (links and brief descriptions)
   - Welcome note template (manager) — includes role expectations and first-week checklist.
   - Rotation kickoff doc template — objective, success metrics, owner contact list.
   - Promotion packet template — evidence checklist and attestation forms.

Ownership and escalation:
- Program owner: People-ops (Priya Desai).
- Tooling and entitlement owner: Eng-Auth (for access flow) and Eng-SRE (for infra).
- Escalation path: manager -> people-ops -> infra lead -> head of eng platform.

Appendix: example 30/60/90 template (plain text)
- 30 days: complete dev environment, merge first non-trivial PR, learn codebase areas X/Y.
- 60 days: independently own a small feature, present a design review, start mentorship sessions.
- 90 days: deliver impact metric, prepare promotion-readiness notes or next-career-growth plan.
